stem: A company runs a web application on one Amazon EC2 instance. The application stores its data in files on the Amazon EBS volume of the instance and cannot run as several copies. During the day the load changes often, and at peaks the CPU utilization of the instance reaches 100%. Users then see slow responses. The company expects the number of users to grow during the next year. The application must handle the growth and the daily peaks with minimal downtime. Which solution will meet these requirements?
keywords: stores its data in files on the Amazon EBS volume of the instance and cannot run as several copies
at peaks the CPU utilization of the instance reaches 100%

options.text: Change the instance to a larger instance type with more vCPUs and more memory while the instance keeps running, so that the users see no interruption.
options.why: To change the instance type, [you must stop your instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-vertical-stop-required), so a resize with no interruption is not possible.

options.text: Run the application in an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer, with a target tracking scaling policy on CPU utilization.
options.why: Each instance that the group launches is another copy, and [data is not automatically copied](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-data-not-copied-to-new-instances) to it, so the files stay on the first instance.

options.text: Stop the instance, change it to a larger instance type with more vCPUs and more memory, and start the instance again.
options.why: It runs as one copy, so a larger type adds vCPUs and memory; [you must stop your instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-vertical-stop-required) to change the type, so one planned stop is the least downtime that works.

options.text: Attach a second elastic network interface to the instance, so that the instance can accept twice as many user requests during the peaks.
options.why: The option repeats the peaks of the stem, but a second network interface adds a network path, not vCPUs, so the CPU utilization still reaches 100% at the peaks.

explanation: The application keeps its files on one instance and cannot run as several copies, and [data is not automatically copied](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-faq-data-not-copied-to-new-instances) to new instances, so a group does not fit. More vCPUs and memory come from a larger instance type. To change the type, [you must stop your instance](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-vertical-stop-required), so [plan for downtime](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-vertical-stop-required): one planned stop is the least downtime of the options that work.
takeaway: When the application runs as a single copy, move it to a larger instance type in one planned stop.
twin: If the stem said "a stateless web application" instead: an Auto Scaling group behind a load balancer, because adding instances is [essential for dynamic workloads with fluctuating demands](../facts/ec2-auto-scaling.md#ec2-auto-scaling-decision-guide-horizontal-for-fluctuating).
say: It runs as one copy, so I'd move it once to a larger instance type and plan one short stop.
